clue.text: Retractable shutter, a novel puzzle

indicators.note: something retractable is drawn back, so the word for the shutter is read from its end to its start

parts.note: a lid shuts a box or pot
Emma is the novel by Jane Austen

explanation.surface: An advert for a puzzle box with a sliding shutter, sold alongside a novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A quandary with no comfortable way out is a puzzle in the sense of a perplexing problem.

clue.text: Head of state locked in warehouse, the tyrant

indicators.note: a thing locked in a building is enclosed by it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a depot is a storage warehouse

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A deposed head of state imprisoned in a warehouse by rebels.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruler with absolute power who uses it cruelly is a tyrant; the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Teaser that's funny, I thank you!

parts.note: LOL, laughing out loud, is text-speak for finding something funny
ta is informal British for thank you

explanation.surface: Someone laughs off a teasing joke and thanks the joker.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the Nabokov novel's title character, whose name became a byword for a precociously flirtatious girl.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of Nabokov's heroine is used for a young girl seen as a flirtatious tease.

clue.text: Dog, pooch struggling to eat new cut of meat

parts.note: a mutt is a mongrel dog

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so one piece goes within the other
the letters of pooch are thrashing about into a new order

explanation.surface: A dog and a pooch fighting to get at a fresh cut of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' rearranges POOCH to OCHOP, and 'to eat' puts N inside it after the first O.
explanation.definitionFit: A chop is a cut of meat with a bone, and one from a sheep carries the name of mature sheep meat.

clue.text: Vital channel in that road going north

indicators.note: going north says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the answer sits inside the words that road

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A main artery of traffic heading north along that road.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft named no indicator for the hidden word; 'in' is it. In a down clue 'going north' reads ATROA upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The great artery carrying blood out of the heart is a channel vital to life.

clue.text: Suspect bows on receiving jihadi leader, flattering to deceive

indicators.note: receiving takes something in, so the letter goes inside the rearranged letters
suspect as an adjective means dubious, so the letters of bows on are not to be trusted in their order
a word's leader is its first letter

explanation.surface: A suspect bows down before a jihadi leader to win favour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suspect' rearranges BOWS ON to SNOWOB, and J goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A persuasive deception built on flattery and smooth talk is American slang for exactly this kind of con.

clue.text: Join past a network of roads?

parts.note: the two words run together read as pasta, and spaghetti is a pasta
a junction is where things join

explanation.surface: An instruction to go on and join something beyond a point.
explanation.walkthrough: Run 'past a' together to get pasta. The answer is the nickname of the tangled Gravelly Hill motorway interchange in Birmingham, England.
explanation.definitionFit: The nickname describes a tangle of looping roads that resemble a plate of pasta strands.

clue.text: Doubly right, a vegetable

parts.note: right twice over: once as OK, meaning correct, and once as R, the abbreviation for right
right twice over: once as OK, meaning correct, and once as R, the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone confirms twice over that a vegetable is correct.
explanation.definitionFit: The green seed pods also called ladies' fingers are eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: See 5
Abroad, well rested, rising every two years

parts.note: bien is French for well, and abroad says a foreign word is wanted

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: lain is the past participle of lie, to rest

explanation.surface: A traveller abroad, well rested, getting up for a trip taken every other year.
explanation.definitionFit: The prefix bi- means two and -ennial means years, so it describes something recurring at two-year intervals.

clue.text: Go__ran Ivan__isevic?

parts.note: the tennis player's name is printed with gaps in it, divided in two, and he was famous for describing his own good and bad sides

explanation.surface: The Croatian tennis player's name, printed broken in two.
explanation.walkthrough: Goran Ivanisevic, the 2001 Wimbledon champion, joked about his 'good Goran' and 'bad Goran'; here his name is literally divided.
explanation.definitionFit: A disorder of two distinct selves fits a man famous for two moods, and a name visibly broken apart.

clue.text: Selection of peaks on the bottom to shift round

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece on another follows it, so the peaks come after the bottom

parts.note: rear is a polite word for the bottom
a range is a series of mountain peaks

explanation.surface: A climber with sore buttocks choosing mountains, told to shift position.
explanation.definitionFit: To shift things round is to put them in a different order, the verb's ordinary sense.

clue.text: Mashed potatoes, healthy skin treatment

indicators.note: mashed food is crushed out of shape, so the letters of potatoes are rearranged
a word's skin is its outermost letters

explanation.surface: Mashed potatoes recommended as a healthy remedy for the skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mashed' makes OSTEOPAT from POTATOES; 'skin' gives HY, the outer letters of 'healthy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Manipulating bones and muscles to relieve pain is a form of medical therapy.

clue.text: Rock loco rolled over

indicators.note: something rolled over is upside down, so the word for loco is turned back to front

parts.note: loco is slang for crazy, as is nuts

explanation.surface: A crazy locomotive rolling over on a rocky stretch of line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loco' looks like a train but is the slang adjective for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: To rock someone is to shock or stagger them, a synonym of the verb meaning to daze.

clue.text: Fake Lowry had a name on it — another artist?

indicators.note: a fake is not genuine, so the letters are rearranged into something new

explanation.surface: A forged Lowry painting with a name signed on it, suggesting a different painter.
explanation.walkthrough: L. S. Lowry was an English painter of northern industrial scenes, hence 'another artist'.
explanation.definitionFit: The American pop artist famous for soup cans is a painter other than Lowry, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Boobs depicted in brief bikini on bird in US city

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece on another follows it

parts.note: a chat is a small songbird such as the stonechat

indicators.note: in places the pair of letters inside the swimwear

parts.note: a tanga is a skimpy, brief style of bikini
two round O letters side by side are a cartoon picture of a pair of breasts

explanation.surface: A saucy picture of a woman in a skimpy bikini posing beside a bird, somewhere in America.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tennessee city famed for the Chattanooga Choo Choo is a city of the United States.

clue.text: Leader in Iran greeting runner, a revolutionary

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns round, so the whole string of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: hallo is a greeting, a variant of hello
a river runs, and the Tay is a river in Scotland

explanation.surface: An Iranian leader greeting a running revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns HALLOTAYA round; the political sense makes it look like a description of the leader.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior Shia cleric, the title held by Iran's supreme leaders Khomeini and Khamenei.

clue.text: Modern thinker, gathering speed

indicators.note: gathering takes something in, so the word for speed sits inside the word for thinker

parts.note: a sage is a wise thinker
pace is speed

explanation.surface: A modern philosopher whose ideas are gaining speed.
explanation.definitionFit: The era of space travel stands for the very latest technology, so used as an adjective it means ultra-modern.

clue.text: Race in short cap, brown on top?

indicators.note: in says the race sits inside the shortened word
short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: to cap something is to better it
a run is a race

explanation.surface: A runner in a short cap, with brown showing on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cap' looks like a hat but is the verb meaning to outdo; cut short, BETTER loses its last letter R.
explanation.definitionFit: A person with brown hair is brown on top, which the question mark signals as a playful definition.

clue.text: See 9
Plan a class for the audience

indicators.note: what an audience gets is heard, so the word is identified by how it is said

parts.note: a gender is a class, as in grammar where nouns fall into gender classes

explanation.surface: A schedule drawn up for a class performing to an audience.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent 'a gender' is said like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A list of items to be dealt with at a meeting is its plan or schedule.

clue.text: See 23
99 in this — or two more?

definitions.meaning: a 99 is a British ice cream, a soft whippy ... with a chocolate flake stuck in it
add two to 99 and get 101, which is C, Roman for a hundred, followed by the word for 1

explanation.surface: A riddle about the number 99 and what follows it.
explanation.walkthrough: A 99 is the British soft ice cream with a chocolate flake; the second reading counts on to 101 as C plus ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: The wafer holder of a 99 ice cream, and the Roman hundred followed by one, both spell the same word.

clue.text: Reformer inhaling grass? One's hooked!

indicators.note: inhaling draws something inside, so the grass goes within the word for reformer

parts.note: a changer is one who changes or reforms
oat is a cereal grass

explanation.surface: A reformer smoking grass has become an addict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's hooked!' looks like a line about addiction to the grass; the answer is a household item with a hook on top.
explanation.definitionFit: The wardrobe item for hanging clothes has a hook at the top, so it is literally hooked.

clue.text: Adjustable borer and widget for adjustable spanner?

indicators.note: something adjustable can be altered, so the letters of borer and widget are rearranged

explanation.surface: A toolkit list: an adjustable drill, a gadget, and a wrench.
explanation.walkthrough: The London landmark over the Thames is a bascule bridge whose roadway lifts, so it is a 'spanner' that adjusts.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridge spans a river, and this London one raises its two halves, making it an adjustable span.

clue.text: Given note for tuning up, then tune up for song

parts.note: an orchestra tunes to the note A given by the oboe

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: an air is a tune

explanation.surface: A musician given a tuning note, then tuning up to sing.
explanation.definitionFit: An operatic solo for one voice is a type of song.

clue.text: Bursting, flow with great warm feeling

indicators.note: bursting breaks apart, so the letters of flow and great are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A great warm feeling bursting out in a flow of emotion.
explanation.definitionFit: The pleasant feeling left after a good experience is a lingering warm glow of satisfaction.

clue.text: Polished diamonds alongside white castle?

indicators.note: alongside says the diamonds sit next to the castle, here placed after it

parts.note: in chess, white's castle (rook) starts on the square h1, written out as h-one
D is the card-playing abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: Polished diamonds displayed beside a white castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'white castle' looks like a building; it is the chess rook on square h1.
explanation.definitionFit: A blade sharpened on a whetstone is polished in the sense of refined and perfected.

clue.text: A solution that's nonsense?

definitions.meaning: a lotion for bathing the eyes is a liquid solution
rubbish talk meant to deceive, as in 'that's all hogwash'

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses an answer as nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a liquid for rinsing the eyes; the other is claptrap or humbug.

clue.text: Publish charter on outsiders in race

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece on another follows it, so the charter comes second
the outsiders of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: to charter something is to hire or lease it

explanation.surface: Publishing a charter on behalf of outsiders in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outsiders' suggests rank horses in a race, but it means the outside letters R and E.
explanation.definitionFit: To put out a record or book to the public is to publish it.
